planting.note: Start seed indoors 6 weeks before the last frost; Super Sioux was bred to keep setting fruit and resist cracking through extreme heat, making it well suited to a Gulf South spring crop.

directions: Super Sioux is a semi-determinate heirloom tomato bred in 1944 at South Dakota State University specifically to withstand extreme heat and resist fruit cracking, qualities that made it a favorite far beyond its Great Plains origin in hot, humid regions such as the Gulf South. The compact plants set medium-sized, 6-8 ounce red fruit with good flavor even when summer nights stay warm enough to shut down fruit set in less heat-tolerant varieties. Stake or cage plants for support and maintain even soil moisture to minimize blossom end rot and cracking during heavy summer rains.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; this University of Florida release was bred specifically to keep setting fruit through Deep South heat and humidity.

directions: Homestead 61 is a determinate open-pollinated tomato released by the University of Florida in 1961 as an improved selection of the earlier Homestead 24, developed specifically for growers in Florida and the Gulf South who needed a tomato that would keep producing through intense heat and humidity without the blossom drop that plagues many standard varieties. Fruits are large, firm, and meaty with good disease tolerance for its era, and the variety became a long-standing dooryard and small-farm standard across the Deep South. Stake plants for cleaner fruit and better airflow in humid gardens, and maintain even watering to reduce cracking.

planting.note: Sow in late summer for a fall-through-winter Gulf South crop, or in early spring; a light frost sweetens the leaves.

directions: Tiger Collard is an African American heritage collard distinguished by its dramatically frilled, deeply serrated leaf margins that give the plant its striped, tiger-like appearance. It was preserved within Southern seed-keeping networks and has more recently been distributed by seed companies working to document and conserve distinct family collard lines, including through the Heirloom Collards Project. The plant is vigorous and productive, tolerating both summer heat and winter cold well enough to provide greens across much of the year in zone 8-10 gardens, and its ruffled texture holds up well when cooked low and slow in traditional Southern style.

planting.note: Start indoors 6 weeks before transplanting; bred in Florida for heavy paste-tomato yields under Gulf South heat and disease pressure.

directions: BHN 444 is a determinate Roma-type hybrid tomato bred by BHN Seed Company of Immokalee, Florida specifically for commercial and garden production in Florida and the broader Gulf South. It carries resistance to Fusarium wilt races 1, 2, and 3, Verticillium wilt, and Gray Leaf Spot, diseases that are common in the region's hot, humid soils, and sets heavy clusters of firm, thick-walled paste fruit well suited to sauce and canning. Stake or support the compact plants to keep fruit off the soil, and harvest regularly through the season for the best continuous yield.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; a University of Florida release bred to perform through Gulf South heat and humidity.

directions: Manapal is an indeterminate slicing tomato released by the University of Florida in the early 1960s, carrying resistance to Verticillium and Fusarium wilt and bred specifically for the hot, humid growing conditions of Florida and the Gulf Coast. It became a widely grown dooryard and market tomato across the Deep South for decades thanks to its large, smooth, flavorful fruit and dependable fruit set during warm nights that stall many Northern-bred varieties. Stake or cage the vigorous vines and provide consistent moisture to reduce cracking and blossom end rot.

planting.note: Start indoors 6 weeks before transplanting; an AAS Gold Medal winner bred by the University of Florida for disease resistance and fruit set under Southern heat and humidity.

directions: Floramerica is a globe-shaped slicing tomato bred by the University of Florida and named an All-America Selections Gold Medal winner in 1978, a distinction awarded only rarely to tomatoes. It carries resistance to Verticillium wilt, Fusarium wilt, and nematodes (VFN), a disease package assembled specifically to help it perform reliably in the hot, humid, nematode-prone soils of Florida and the Gulf South. The semi-determinate plants produce heavy clusters of smooth, deep-red, well-flavored fruit over a long summer season. Stake plants and water evenly to minimize blossom end rot during the region's alternating heavy rain and dry spells.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; one of the foundational University of Florida heat- and disease-tolerant slicing tomatoes for Gulf South gardens.

directions: Floradel is a large-fruited slicing tomato released by the University of Florida in the late 1950s, bred with Verticillium and Fusarium wilt resistance for growers facing the heat, humidity, and soilborne disease pressure of Florida and the broader Gulf South. It was an early link in a long chain of Florida tomato breeding that went on to produce related heat-adapted varieties such as Manalucie and Manapal, and it remained a dependable market and dooryard tomato for Southern gardeners for years after its release. Stake or cage the vigorous plants and keep moisture consistent to limit cracking and blossom end rot.
